proof_summary: The block \([2,4,2,4,2]\) beginning at index \(3\) can occur only once: an occurrence would make \(q,q+2,q+6,q+8,q+12,q+14\) all prime, but these numbers cover every residue modulo \(5\), so one must equal \(5\). The resulting cases force \(q=5\) and hence the original starting index (while \(q=3\) would require \(9\) to be prime), proving uniqueness rather than infinite recurrence.
